Microsoft Quarterly Profit Soars as Cloud Growth Accelerates — WSJ

The 48% growth in the Azure cloud business propelled Microsoft's revenue to $92.28 billion, up 19%, for its fiscal first quarter. The result handily beat Wall Street's expectations for $90.62 billion in revenue, according to analysts polled by FactSet.

The new Agent and Infra segment, which includes revenue from Azure and Microsoft 365 products among other sources, contributed $76.8 billion in revenue to that total. Microsoft revamped its reporting segments in September.

Microsoft logged a profit of $36.63 billion, or $4.92 a share, up from $27.75 billion, or $3.72 a share, a year earlier. On an adjusted basis, earnings were $4.89 a share, ahead of the $4.71 analysts were expecting.
